problem: Existing object-driven navigation benchmarks target generic categories or objects frozen in the scanned scene, so they cannot test whether an agent finds a specific personal instance among same-category distractors that can appear anywhere.
motivation: A home robot asked to fetch a particular teddy bear must tell it apart from similar toys, and personal objects move around, so scene context and location priors are unreliable. No benchmark combines photo-realistic scenes, injected movable objects, multimodal (image and text) references and same-category distractors.
key_idea: Introduce the Personalized Instance-based Navigation (PIN) task and the PInNED dataset, which injects 338 Objaverse-XL objects into HM3D scenes with same-category distractors and gives the target as neutral-background images plus manual text descriptions.
insight: Same-category distractors are the core difficulty: removing them raises DINOv2 modular SR from 14.84 to 23.13, and the per-category analysis links intra-category similarity to category errors, since a single similarity threshold cannot separate instances. Small objects (keys, wallet, watch) get 0% SR, while the best end-to-end agents lag behind the best modular ones. Replacing fine-grained descriptions with plain category names barely changes CLIP/OWL SR (3.52 vs 3.10; 7.79 vs 7.29), showing that vision-language models ignore fine-grained detail.
method: Task definition: the agent starts at a random pose in an unseen HM3D scene and must stop within 1 m of the target instance in at most 1000 steps. Actions are stop, move ahead 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, tilt up/down 30°. The target is given as 3 neutral-background renders and 3 text descriptions.

PInNED dataset: 338 Objaverse-XL objects in 18 categories, manually rescaled. Objects are spawned on HM3D surfaces such as sofa, bed, table and cabinet. Each episode has up to 6 same-category and up to 13 other-category distractors. There are 865,519 train and 1,193 val episodes, with disjoint train/val object instances (266/72).
Modular agent - exploration and exploitation: frontier-based exploration builds an occupancy map, and once the goal is detected, Fast Marching Method planning goes to the projected goal position.

Modular agent - detection module: it returns a matching score against a threshold plus goal coordinates. Three families are tested: keypoint matching (SuperGlue, IEVE with GroundedSAM + LightGlue/DISK), patch-level ViT similarity (DINO, DINOv2, CLIP, CLIP-Grad), and detectors (PerSAM, PerSAM-F, OWL).

End-to-end agents: RIM is fine-tuned with behavior cloning from ObjectNav weights, with the category embedding replaced by mean CLIP features of visual or textual references. ZSON is fine-tuned with RL from ImageNav pretraining using reference images.
Metrics: SR, SPL, D2G, steps, plus the proposed Category Error (CE, the share of episodes stopped within 1 m of a same-category distractor) and detection metrics %Match, TM, CM and NM.

setting.backbone: Modular: frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 (best), CLIP, DINO, OWL, SuperGlue, PerSAM, IEVE with thresholds tuned on training episodes; end-to-end: RIM and ZSON (ResNet-50) fine-tuned
setting.training_data: Modular agents are training-free apart from threshold tuning on a subset of training episodes. RIM and ZSON are fine-tuned on the 865.5k PInNED training episodes (RIM ~2M steps, ZSON ~5M steps).
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (360x640, hfov 42) + depth, with pose for the mapping and RIM agents
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: stop, move ahead 0.25 m, turn ±30°, tilt ±30°
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes with injected Objaverse-XL objects)
setting.privileged: none (object category labels exist in the data but are not to be used by the agent)

numbers.extra: same-category distractors present; 1000 step budget; threshold tuned on train subset; 1 m success radius

numbers_note: The paper is a benchmark paper; only baselines adapted by the authors are reported. Numbers above are for the with-distractor setting (Table 1). The no-distractor ablation (Table 2) gives DINOv2 SR 23.13 / SPL 11.61.
results: On PInNED the best baseline, the modular DINOv2 agent with visual references, reaches only 14.84 SR / 7.94 SPL, and the best end-to-end agent (ZSON) 9.14 SR / 7.18 SPL. Modular agents generally beat end-to-end ones, but the task remains far from solved, with keys, wallet and watch never succeeding.
limitations: Small or detailed objects degrade in simulator rendering and are nearly undetectable from a distance (0% SR on keys, wallet and watch).
Only a validation split exists (no test split), because HM3D test scene access is missing; results use a single threshold per backbone and only baselines are evaluated, with no new method proposed.
Evaluation is simulation-only, and object placement uses a fixed set of surfaces; modular evaluation is slow (~44 GPU hours per run).
